facts.statement: The genus Breagyps is named after the La Brea Tar Pits in California, where its fossils were found.
facts.quote: The genus takes its name from the La Brea Tar Pits in California, where its remains have been recovered.

facts.statement: Breagyps is an extinct genus of New World vulture belonging to the family Cathartidae.
facts.quote: Breagyps is an extinct genus of New World vulture in the family Cathartidae.

facts.statement: The only known species in the genus is Breagyps clarki.
Breagyps lived from the Chibanian to the Late Pleistocene, between 0.21 and 0.0117 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Chibanian to Late Pleistocene (0.21 to 0.0117 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Breagyps clarki is one of three vulture species known from La Brea Tar Pits fossils, alongside the living Turkey vulture.
rejected.quote: Breagyps clarki is one of three vulture species represented by fossil material from the tar pits, including the extant Turkey vulture.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Breagyps clarki is one of three vulture species'
